FROM PIXELS TO YOUR DESK

Hardware concept

Prototype → physical companion

  1. Start on USB power with an ESP32-S3 development board, a compatible I²C display, and an SHT40 or BME280 breakout.
  2. Share ground and verify each breakout’s voltage and pull-ups. Choose GPIO pins from your exact board’s pinout; this concept does not assign universal pins.
  3. Add WS2812 LEDs with suitable power, a data resistor, and level shifting where required. Add a presence sensor for reliable presence detection.
  4. Build clock and sensor firmware first. Add Wi-Fi weather and an authenticated model backend later; keep API keys off the public website.
  5. Only add a LiPo using a protected cell and a compatible charging/power-path board. Validate power and enclosure clearance before building.

Visual enclosure concept, not production CAD or an electrically validated schematic. Weather, sensor values, and voice events are simulated; no microphone or camera is accessed.
